title_as_printed: Experimental Data in Two-Phase Region (Concentration of water in propane-rich phases)
pressure_note: Column 'Pressure, Lb./Sq. Inch Abs.' (absolute, total equilibrium cell pressure, as measured on gauges)

value.col: Composition of propane-rich phase mole fraction water
value.what: mole fraction water in the propane-rich phase (vapor or liquid depending on row, see overrides)

composition.other_species: pure water; propane stated as not less than 99 mole %

conversion_needs: psia and F conversion; propane mole fraction is on a total basis (water-rich liquid: propane per total moles of liquid)
notes: Isotherms 100, 150, 190, 205.7, 230, 260, 300 F; blocks separated by a blank line in print (no label rows). Replicate-looking rows (100 F/2798 psia; 260 F/2023 psia) are distinct printed values, kept.

row_regime_overrides.reason: pressure above the three-phase pressure at that temperature (Table I/IV: 191.5 psia at 100 F, about 311-389 psia at 140-160 F, 538 psia at 190 F), so the propane-rich phase is liquid; rows below are vapor (regime empty); at 205.7 F and above (T >= propane Tc about 206 F) no liquid/vapor distinction is made. This classification is the extractor's inference from the paper's own three-phase data, the paper does not label rows.

row_held.reason: probable printed misprint: 0.00492 at 100 F / 533 psia is about 8x the neighbouring liquid values (0.000587 at 818 psia; Table V p.444 gives 0.000604 at 500 psia, 100 F); probably 0.000492; cell not changed

quality_remarks: Row 2 (100 F, 533 psia, 0.00492) is a probable misprint of 0.000492 (see row_held).
